summary:
### Regulations
Regulatory classification: transparency_obligated  
The AI feature that answers billing questions does not fall under any provisions of Annex III and is therefore not classified as high-risk. However, Article 50(1) of the EU AI Act governs it to the extent that the feature interacts directly with natural persons. This obliges the provider to inform the person they are interacting with an AI system, unless it is already obvious in context. No other applicable or specific obligations for this feature were identified in the retrieved provisions.  
This is AI-generated regulatory analysis, not legal advice. Review with Legal before acting on it, especially for 'prohibited' or 'high_risk' classifications.

Applicability: Under Article 113, the provisions cited here take effect on these dates: 2 August 2026 (Article 50; the general application date).

### Overview  
5 of 102 configurations meet the latency and budget targets you gave. Latency here means the time until the first answer token arrives (the reply starts appearing). 66 could not be compared on latency because no timing data exists for them. Costs assume 20,000 requests a month, because no volume was given, with 1,500 input and 250 output tokens each (token sizes estimated from the kind of feature).  

### Warnings  
- Token sizes were outside the typical range for a chat assistant and were moved to the nearest end of it (input tokens 200 -> 1,500).  
- The feature was read as a chat assistant but its reply style as a single response; treated as a streamed chat.  
- OpenAI: rejected 3 of 40 extracted models (gpt-6-1-sol: model name not on the page; davinci-002: not a text-generation model (by name); babbage-002: not a text-generation model (by name)).  
- Google: rejected 15 of 23 extracted models (gemini-3.5-flash-lite: input price not found with the model's name on the page; gemini-3.8-live: not a text-generation model (by name); gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking: not a text-generation model (by name); gemini-3.1-flash: model name not on the page).

quotes.label: Article 50(1)
quotes.title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
quotes.text: 1. Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect, taking into account the circumstances and the context of use. This obligation shall not apply to AI systems authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences, subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties, unless those systems are available for the public to report a criminal offence.
